steps.action: Posed the unresolved tectonic setting and formation age of the Lüliangshan VMS-type Cu deposit as the question.
steps.quote: However, the tectonic setting and age of related VMS deposits remain debated.

steps.action: Listed published rivals: late Cambrian, middle Ordovician or Silurian ages, and backarc, continental arc or island arc settings.
steps.quote: many researchers have proposed that the Lüliangshan Cu deposit formed in a backarc basin

steps.action: Described field relations, lithologies and petrography of the ore-hosting volcano-sedimentary rocks and surrounding mafic-ultramafic rocks as a possible ophiolite complex.
steps.quote: Abundant meta-gabbro and meta-dolerite dykes with a width of a few meters to tens of meters are also observed within the Tanjianshan Group

steps.action: Analysed whole-rock major and trace elements (XRF, ICP-MS) of eight greenschist samples collected far from the orebody.
steps.quote: Eight greenschist samples were selected for major and trace element analysis.

steps.action: Checked that REE and HFSE correlate with immobile Zr and Y to argue the compositions are not altered, and based interpretation on immobile elements.
steps.quote: show good correlations with immobile elements (e.g., Zr, Y) (not shown), indicating little affection by seafloor alteration or metamorphism

steps.action: Took discrimination fields and reference patterns (N-MORB, IBM forearc basalt, IBM boninite, chert environment fields) from published work as expectations for each setting.
steps.quote: Izu-Bonin-Mariana (IBM) forearc basalts are from Reagan et al. (2010); IBM boninites are from Shervais et al. (2021)

steps.action: Compared greenschist compositions with the discrimination fields and N-MORB, finding tholeiitic, IAT-like signatures.
steps.quote: In the YbN versus DyN plot, they fall within the field of island arc tholeiite (IAT)

steps.action: Compiled published geochemical data for amphibolites, meta-dolerites, boninitic lavas and cherts of the same complex.
steps.quote: Data sources: amphibolites are from Zhou et al. (2019); dolerites are from Fu et al. (2022); boninites are from Tuo (2019)

steps.action: Compared the compiled rocks with reference fields: amphibolite and meta-dolerite as forearc basalt, Kaipinggou lavas as boninite, cherts as hydrothermal iron-rich.
steps.quote: These are considered as the typical geochemical features of forearc basalt (FAB)

steps.action: Measured whole-rock Sr-Nd isotopes on three greenschists, calculated at 520 Ma.
steps.quote: Three greenschist from the Lüliangshan copper deposit were selected for whole-rock Sr-Nd isotopes.

steps.action: Dated zircons from two meta-gabbros intruding the ore-hosting lavas by LA-ICP-MS, giving weighted mean ages of 523 ± 3 and 518 ± 3 Ma.
steps.quote: Eighteen grains yield concordant 206Pb/238U ages ranging from 513 to 535 Ma and a weighted mean 206Pb/238U age of 523 ± 3 Ma

steps.action: Measured zircon Lu-Hf isotopes on the dated grains (positive εHf(t)).
steps.quote: Five zircons were selected for Lu-Hf isotopic analysis.

steps.action: Checked the isotope measurements against reference standards (NBS987, GSB-Nd, GJ-1 zircon matching the published value); reported in Analytical methods.
steps.quote: which coincides with that reported by Elhlou et al. (2006)

steps.action: Interpreted petrogenesis: forearc-like high-Cr chromite (cited data), FAB from depleted mantle with hydrous fluids, greenschists with more SSZ input, boninites from residual mantle, cherts ridge-proximal and subduction-related.
steps.quote: suggesting that more SSZ components were involved in their magma source

steps.action: Compared the rock assemblage and the FAB-boninite-IAT progression with IBM forearc, Oman and Hellenide ophiolites formed during subduction initiation.
steps.quote: These rocks, especially high-Cr chromitites, FAB, and boninite, are consistent with those in IBM forearc and Oman

steps.action: Placed the ophiolite in an intra-oceanic trench-arc architecture next to the Nanshan accretionary complex identified in the authors' earlier work.
steps.quote: An accretionary complex was identified in the Nanshan area to the south of ophiolitic rocks

steps.action: Kept the forearc-setting interpretation for the ophiolite and the Cu deposit.
steps.quote: Therefore, we proposed that the ophiolite and Lüliangshan Cu deposit were formed in forearc setting.

steps.action: Combined the new ages with published gabbro and plagiogranite ages to bracket the ophiolite and argue the host rocks predate or are coeval with the meta-gabbros (527–518 Ma).
steps.quote: the prevalent ages of Luofengpo ophiolite are bracketed to 527∼506 Ma

steps.action: Used the published short duration of subduction initiation and the oldest regional island-arc age (514 ± 8 Ma) as timing expectations.
steps.quote: Initial subduction is a short-lived process (7∼10 m.y.)

steps.action: Constrained initial Proto-Tethyan subduction to ca. 530–520 Ma.
steps.quote: the initial subduction of Proto-Tethys Ocean can be constrained at ca. 530∼520 Ma

steps.action: Kept the claim that the Cu deposit formed during early Cambrian forearc spreading.
steps.quote: [...] Cu deposit formed during the forearc spreading in the early Cambrian

tree.answer: An ophiolite-hosted VMS Cu deposit whose setting and age are disputed
No; setting and age are inferred from host-rock geochemistry and zircon dating of intruding gabbros
Constrain the tectonic setting and formation age of the deposit
Backarc, continental arc, island arc versus forearc; late Cambrian, middle Ordovician, Silurian ages
Discrimination diagrams and modern analog (IBM) compositions differ by setting
Conditions found in rock traces, not set
Only an alteration check and analytical standards; no sensitivity tests or independent dating of the ore
Forearc, early Cambrian setting kept as best explanation

end.claim: The Lüliangshan Cu deposit is an ophiolite-hosted VMS deposit that formed in a forearc spreading setting in the early Cambrian, during early-stage subduction of the Proto-Tethys Ocean.

decisive_move.sentence: Matching the assemblage of high-Cr chromitite, forearc basalt, boninite and IAT to the IBM forearc and Oman analogs is what turns scattered geochemical signatures into the forearc-setting claim.

gates.evidence: The ophiolite-hosted framing in the Introduction (p. 2) guided sampling of greenschists and intruding meta-gabbros, but no setting hypothesis was stated before data collection. Samples could have plotted in backarc or MORB fields, but the backarc rival is never explicitly tested or excluded. Nothing was fixed before the data.

X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (XRF-1800) for major elements
Wet chemical volumetric titration for FeO
Multi-collector ICP-MS (Neptune Plus) with laser ablation for Sr-Nd and Hf isotopes

limits: The supplied XML text holds only the abstract and captions, so body text is cited by printed journal pages. No review file was supplied; the acknowledgments thank a guest editor and anonymous reviewers, but what they changed is unknown. New data are limited to eight greenschists, three Sr-Nd analyses and two zircon samples. Most of the setting evidence (chromite, chert, boninite, amphibolite, dolerite) is taken from published work, part of it the authors' own (Fu et al., 2022). The backarc rival named in the Introduction is not revisited or explicitly excluded in the Discussion (inference). The deposit age is not measured directly; it is inferred from intruding gabbros (a minimum age) plus a timing argument from cited subduction-initiation durations. The alteration check relies on correlations 'not shown'. Sub-claims at other statuses: meta-gabbro ages 523 ± 3 and 518 ± 3 Ma (estimate_with_resolution); ophiolite-hosted classification of the deposit (best_explanation); initial subduction at ca. 530–520 Ma (best_explanation).

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Mobile elements such as LOI, SiO2 and LILEs

alternatives_considered.chosen: Relatively fresh samples collected far from the orebody, without secondary veins
alternatives_considered.reason: To minimize the influence of alteration

alternatives_considered.chosen: Bracketing the deposit age by dating meta-gabbros intruding the host rocks and using related rocks
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Directly dating the volcano-sedimentary host rocks
alternatives_considered.reason: Wide age range of the Tanjianshan Group and difficulty dating volcano-sedimentary rocks
